chunks: And from him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you stand for the prayer and say Takbir, raise your hands, and do not let your palms exceed your ears, i.e., parallel to your cheeks.

key_terms.فَكَبَّرْتَ: When you say Takbir (exclaiming Allahu Akbar)

ai.seo_question: How high should one raise their hands during the opening Takbir of Salat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Al-Kafi* establishes the precise physical limit for *raf' al-yadayn* during the opening Takbir, specifying that hands should not exceed the earlobes but rather align with the cheeks. This detail is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing the recommended practice from other schools that may raise hands higher or lower, emphasizing modesty and uniformity in ritual posture. The chain of transmission highlights the direct link to the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the authority of their specific ritual instructions.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you stand regarding the Salāt and you exclaim Takbīr, so raise your hands, and your palms should not exceed your ears, i.e. parallel to your cheeks’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When you stand up for Salah (prayer) say Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) and raise your hands. Do not allow your palms (hands) to rise higher than your ears. Keep them on the sides of your face.’”
